cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Stay for the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm giving you the full account of why I was late to the reunion. Stay here and hear it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saved you a seat beside me. Was it traffic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That explanation isn't approved. I waited outside for half an hour, and I want you to hear why.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm here. But I thought you didn't want to sit with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wanted that seat. I was afraid you were happier while it was empty. Now you may take the one beside me and tell me whether you can stay after hearing that.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 orders a full hearing, A3 disallows the easy traffic explanation and A5 grants a nearby seat after the hardest admission, maintaining superior form while testing continued support.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 saved seat/traffic hypothesis causes A3 deliberate-wait truth; B4 rejection interpretation causes A5 fear that B preferred the empty seat.

relationship.evidence: B2 saved a place and B4 stays while naming personal hurt, supplying both support and a reason for deeper honesty.

heightening.evidence: B4 hurt misunderstanding prompts A5 the opposite vulnerable motive and a present test of sitting together.

specificity.evidence: A1 reunion lateness and A3 outside half hour establish behavior; A5 current seat is an offered ordinary place, not an invented special mechanism.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 permission to sit after confessing fear of not being wanted carries restrained status irony.
